newsitem.title: UK: Bulgarian debt default remains real risk -- M.Lynch.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian debt default remains real risk -- M.Lynch.

text.p: There is a real risk that Bulgaria could default next year despite recent attempts to reform the economy as part of an agreement with the International Monetary Fund, Merrill Lynch said on Friday.

"Whilst we believe the government is in principle strongly committed to external debt service, in practice the political trade-off may be a difficult one if the choice is between further bank closures and reneging on some external debt obligations," economist Andrew Kenningham said.
"It is difficult to put a probability on the event occuring but we view it as a genuine risk in 1997," he said in a research paper.

It is too early to say whether the IMF programme can save Bulgaria from deepening economic crisis, with continuing problems such as a high public debt burden, insolvency of the banking system and a weak private sector.

Kenningham said the total burden of public debt may now have reached an unsustainable level of more than 150 percent of gdp and could continue to rise because of deficits in the state enterprise sector.
The IMF programme appears relatively fragile and relies on some rather optimistic assumptions which means kepy macro-economic targets are likely to be missed.
It is also not clear that Bulgaria could rely on increased support from the IMF or World Bank, he added.
